title: Kadai Paneer Gravy
subtitle: A cashew-tomato kadai gravy with fresh-ground masala — no onion, no garlic, full of body.
protein: ~12–14g protein per adult serving — from paneer

method.title: Grind masala, build the base
items: Add coriander seeds {3 tbsp}, Kashmiri chilies {2–3, deseeded}, fennel seeds {1½ tsp}, cardamoms {4–5}, cloves {3}, and cinnamon {¼ in — hard limit, don't increase} to a spice grinder; blitz to a fine-ish powder. No need to roast — set aside.
Heat ghee {1½ tbsp} in a deep pan on medium; add cashews {12} and toast until pale gold, 1–2 min
Add tomatoes {400g, chopped} and salt {¼ tsp}; once softened (3–4 min), stir in tomato paste {2 tbsp}
Cover and cook on medium until completely mushy, 10–12 min
Cool fully, then blend to a smooth paste — no water needed; set aside

method.title: Char the vegetables & paneer
items: Wipe the pan clean; heat ghee {1 tbsp} until smoking on the highest flame
Add celery {2 stalks, sliced} and bell peppers {1½ cups, cubed}; toss constantly 90 sec — charred edges, not steamed
Add paneer {400g, cubed, patted dry}; toss 60–90 sec only — do not overcook
Set aside a small handful of paneer and capsicum separately for the toddler portion
Transfer the rest to a plate and set aside

method.title: Bloom hing, build the masala
items: Add ghee {1 tbsp} to the pan; add hing {¼ tsp} to the cold ghee and let it bloom as the oil heats — it will foam briefly
Add ginger paste {1½ tsp}; sauté on medium 1–2 min until the raw smell fades
Add tomato paste {1 tbsp}; fry 60 sec until it darkens slightly
Add all the kadai masala {from Step 1}; sauté on low-medium 2–3 min until deeply fragrant — don't rush

method.title: Add the base and simmer
items: Add the blended tomato-cashew paste {from Step 1}; sauté 3–4 min until the masala tightens and ghee separates at the sides
Pour in water {1½–2 cups} and salt {1¼ tsp, adjust}; bring to a boil, then simmer 5 min

method.label: Toddler portion — pull before chili powder goes in
items: Right now, before chili powder or garam masala go in: scoop out ½ cup of gravy — hing, ginger, and the tomato-cashew base are all fine for her
Add the paneer and capsicum pieces set aside earlier, plus ½ cup boiled diced carrot or potato
Thin with 2 tbsp water if needed; simmer 1 minute

method.title: Spice and finish the gravy
items: Add Kashmiri chili powder {½ tsp} and garam masala {¾ tsp} to the adult gravy; simmer 3–5 more min until it thickens and oil floats on top
Crush kasuri methi {1½ tsp} between your palms and stir in; taste and adjust salt and garam masala
Optional: stir in heavy cream {3 tbsp} on low heat for a silkier finish
Add the remaining sautéed paneer {rest of the 400g}, capsicum {rest of the 1½ cups} and celery {2 stalks} back into the gravy; stir gently to coat
Turn off the heat; scatter ginger juliennes {½ inch, matchsticks} over the top
Add fresh coriander {3 tbsp, chopped}; cover and rest 2 min — the juliennes bloom in residual heat

method.title: Rest before serving
items: Transfer to a serving vessel; rest at least 15 min off heat — this is when paneer absorbs the masala flavors, don't skip
Serve with fresh roti, paratha, or jeera rice
Reheats well with a splash of water on the stovetop — don't microwave at high power, it toughens the paneer; keeps 3 days refrigerated

method.label: Tip
method.text: You'll use just under half the 170g tomato paste can — refrigerate the rest, it keeps 1–2 weeks. The ginger juliennes at the end aren't redundant with the ginger paste earlier — raw and matchstick-cut, they add a fresh, sharp bite the cooked paste doesn't have.
